text:
I'll start with read-only checks that don't need admin. Setup needs an elevated PowerShell, so I'll give you those commands after you answer the questions below.

**Checks I'd run now (not elevated):**

```powershell
gh auth status
gh api repos/acme/webapp --jq '{private: .private, admin: .permissions.admin}'
Get-Command tentmaker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
tailscale status
```

The `gh api` line shows whether the token has admin on `acme/webapp`. Runner registration needs that. If `admin` is `false`, setup can't register runners with this token.

**Questions before I go further:**

1. **Windows jobs?** A Windows device runs only Windows jobs (`runs-on: [self-hosted, tentmaker, Windows]`). Does `acme/webapp` have Windows jobs? If its CI is Linux or macOS only, this PC adds nothing for that repo.
2. **Public repo?** If `acme/webapp` is public, I need your explicit approval before adding it. That means `--allow-public --enable`, which makes outside contributors need approval before any of their workflows run on your machines.
3. **Broker or worker?** This PC can hold a GitHub token and register runners for `acme/webapp` (broker). Or it can run with no token and take jobs from another device on your tailnet with the same owner and pool name (worker). A broker stores your token in the Windows secret store, so I need your yes before I give this machine a token.
4. **Budget.** Should I use the defaults (a quarter of RAM for everyday use, half for plugged-in boost), or do you want specific limits like `--memory 4GiB --boost-memory 12GiB`?
5. **Tailscale.** Is Tailscale installed and signed in on this PC? If not, install it first. Without it, the device can't join your pool.

**Once you answer, you run these in an elevated PowerShell** (Start, type "PowerShell", Run as administrator):

```powershell
$env:TENTMAKER_NO_SETUP = '1'
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baney75/tentmaker/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
tentmaker setup --yes --json --repo acme/webapp --memory 4GiB --boost-memory 12GiB
tentmaker doctor --json
tentmaker pool --json
```

Drop `--repo acme/webapp` if you choose worker mode. Add `--no-gh` in that case so the machine never holds a token. Drop the `--memory` and `--boost-memory` values if you want the defaults.

Setup restarts the service, so a running job would keep going. Doctor should exit 0 before we call this done. The last step is to point `acme/webapp` at the pool, and only for Windows jobs. I'll make that change only after you approve the diff.
